title: Emperor Penguins Survive -40 Degrees by Never Standing Still

scenes.text: In the Antarctic winter, penguins stay alive by never standing still.
The air in one recording was around minus forty degrees Celsius.
Yet inside the huddle, it climbed above zero, and in places up to thirty-seven degrees.
Every thirty to sixty seconds, the whole crowd takes a tiny step, five to ten centimeters.
That step ripples through the huddle like a wave, so everyone gets a turn in the warm middle.
The males fast for about four months like this. A living, shuffling heater.

description:
In the Antarctic winter, penguins stay alive by never standing still.
A study found emperor penguin huddles pack about 21 birds per square meter and move in slow waves, with temperatures inside reaching up to 37 degrees Celsius.
Could you stand in that crowd?
